Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And God said to him: 'Look — I have made you a master in the matter of Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother shall be your spokesman.'
translations.2: You shall speak to Aaron your brother with all that I command you, and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he may release the sons of Israel from his land.'
translations.3: And I shall harden the heart of Pharaoh, and multiply My signs and My proofs in the land of Egypt.
translations.4: And Pharaoh shall not accept from you, until I bring My plagues upon the Egyptians, and bring forth My hosts — My people, the sons of Israel — from the land of Egypt, with great judgments.
translations.5: And the Egyptians shall know that I am God, when I release My plagues upon them, and bring out the sons of Israel from among them.'
translations.6: And Moses and Aaron did as God had commanded them — so they did.
translations.7: And Moses was eighty years of age, and Aaron eighty-three years of age, when the two of them spoke to Pharaoh.
translations.8: Then God said to Moses and Aaron, saying:
translations.9: 'When Pharaoh speaks to you and says: Give me a proof — then say to Aaron: Take your staff, and throw it before him; it shall become a serpent.'
translations.10: And Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and did so, as God had said; and Aaron threw his staff before Pharaoh and his officers, and it became a serpent.
translations.11: Then Pharaoh called for the sages and the sorcerers; and the learned men of Egypt did the same with their secret arts.
translations.12: Each man threw his staff, and they became like serpents — but Aaron's staff swallowed their staves.
translations.13: And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not accept from them — as God had said.
translations.14: And God said to Moses: 'The heart of Pharaoh has grown heavy, and he has refused to release the people.'
translations.15: 'Go to him in the morning — behold, he is going out to the water — and stand to meet him on the shore of the Nile; and the staff which turned into a serpent, take it in your hand.'
translations.16: 'And say to him: God, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying: Release my people, that they may serve me in the open country — and behold, you have not accepted until now.'
translations.17: 'Thus says God: By this means shall you know that I am God, the One who punishes — behold, I am striking with the staff that is in my hand the water which is in the Nile, and it shall turn to blood.'
translations.18: 'And the fish that are in the Nile shall perish, and the Nile shall stink, and the Egyptians shall be unable to drink water from the Nile.'
translations.19: Then God said to Moses: 'Say to Aaron: Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of the Egyptians — over their rivers and their inlets and their marshes, and the rest of the gatherings of their waters — that they may turn to blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, and in vessels of wood and of stone.'
translations.21: And the fish that were in the Nile perished, and the Nile stank, and the Egyptians were unable to drink water from it; and blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.
translations.22: And the learned men of Egypt did the same with their secret arts; and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not accept from them — as God had said.
translations.23: Then Pharaoh turned away and entered his house, and did not set his mind to this either.
translations.24: And all the Egyptians dug wells around the Nile to drink from them, since they could not bear to drink from the water of the Nile.
translations.25: And when seven days had been completed after God had struck the Nile — thereafter:
translations.26: God said to Moses: 'Go in to Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says God — release my people, that they may serve me.'
translations.27: 'And if you refuse to release them — behold, I am about to strike your territory with frogs.'
translations.28: 'And the frogs shall move forth from the Nile, and shall ascend and enter into your house, and into the inner chamber of your bed and upon your bed, and into your ovens and your kneading-troughs.'
translations.29: 'And upon your person and upon the person of your people and your officers — the frogs shall ascend.'
